'''Puck Naeco''' was a [[human]] [[Gender|male]] [[ace]] [[pilot]] who served in the [[Rebel Alliance Starfighter Corps|Starfighter Corps]] of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] during the early [[Galactic Civil War]]. Flying with both [[Green Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Green]] and later [[Red Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Red Squadrons]], by the time of the [[Battle of Yavin]] he was a veteran pilot and had reached the status of [[Ace|double ace]]. However, he met his demise as Red Squadron fought to destroy the [[Death Star]] at [[Yavin Prime|Yavin]], shot down by the [[Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader's]] [[TIE Advanced x1]].

==Biography==
During the [[Imperial Era]], Puck Naeco joined the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] in its fight against the [[Galactic Empire]], serving as a [[pilot]] in the [[Rebel Alliance Starfighter Corps|Alliance Starfighter Corps]],<ref name="Duty Roster" /> and eventually became a double ace and [[A-wing starfighter|A-wing]] veteran.<ref name="Odyssey">''[[The Odyssey of Star Wars: An Epic Poem]]''</ref> In the [[Standard year|year]] [[1 BBY]],<ref name="RO Date">{{FilmDate|RO}}</ref> Naeco flew in [[Green Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Green Squadron]], under the [[callsign]] [[Green Twelve]]. Before the [[Battle of Scarif]], Naeco broke his ankle in a rough landing forcing him to vacate his spot in Green Squadron. He was replaced as Green Twelve by [[Lieutenant]] [[Wion Dillems]], who flew in this capacity at the Battle of [[Scarif]].<ref name="UVG" />

===Battle of Yavin===
Following his recovery, Naeco became part of [[Red Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Red Squadron]], under [[Red Leader]] [[Commander]] [[Garven Dreis]]<ref name="UVG" /><ref name="Duty Roster" /> The veteran pilot grew to enjoy teasing his younger comrades, which led to friction in the squadron — manifesting itself in several confrontations with [[Col Takbright]].<ref name="Duty Roster" /> During the approach of the [[Death Star]], Naeco, along with his fellow pilots, attended the briefing held by [[General]] [[Jan Dodonna]], where the commander of the [[Massassi Group]] described their objective: destruction of the [[battle station]] via [[Proton torpedo|torpedoing]] of the [[thermal exhaust port]] leading to the station's [[Reactor|main reactor]].<ref name="Duty Roster" /><ref name="ANH" /> Naeco, along with [[Red Four]] [[John D. Branon]], noticed Takbright's outburst criticizing the plan and pressed him on it afterwards.<ref name="Duty Roster" />

Naeco, at this point a [[Ace|double ace]] with 5,879 flight [[Standard hour|hours]] and eleven confirmed kills,<ref name="Grounded">{{StoryCite|story=Grounded|book=From a Certain Point of View}}</ref> was selected by Dreis to fly with him and [[Theron Nett]] in the Red Squadron's [[first flight]], taking the portside position as [[Red Twelve]]. Following the demise of the original flight of [[Gold Squadron]] [[BTL-A4 Y-wing assault starfighter/bomber|Y-wing bombers]] intended to fire the torpedoes, Dreis' flight entered the [[meridian trench]] of the Death Star and prepared to take the shot.<ref name="Duty Roster" /> However, despite the warnings of Red Leader, Naeco's [[T-65B X-wing starfighter|X-wing starfighter]] would be the first destroyed by the [[Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]], as he pursued the flight in his [[TIE Advanced x1]]. His X-Wing exploded, and crashed against the wall of the trench. Both Nett and Dreis were also shot down soon after, though [[Luke Skywalker|Red Five]] was able to successfully take the shot and destroy the station.<ref name="ANH" />

==Equipment==
As part of [[Red Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Red Squadron]], this pilot wore the customary [[Color|Orange]] [[Flight suit|jumpsuit]], and a [[Flight helmet|helmet]]. His skin was light.<ref name="ANH" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|When Red 10 gets shot down, the pilot we see die is someone else – a previously unseen male pilot with a helmet that looks like Janson's in ''The Empire Strikes Back''. That pilot, we decided, should be Red 12.|Jason Fry|<ref name="Notes">{{Tumblr|subdomain=jasonfry|url=post/24614452839/eg-to-warfare-endnotes-pt-10|name=Jason Fry's Dorkery|text=EG to Warfare: Endnotes Pt. 10}}</ref>}}
The character of Puck Naeco was first created by author [[Rusel DeMaria]] in the [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]] book ''[[X-Wing: The Official Strategy Guide]]'', itself based on the [[Star Wars: X-Wing (video game)|''Star Wars: X-Wing'']] [[Star Wars video games|video game]].<ref name="XW:OSG">''[[X-Wing: The Official Strategy Guide]]''</ref> In ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'', [[Jason Fry]] and [[Paul R. Urquhart|Paul Urquhart]] [[Retroactive continuity|retconned]] the [[Puck Naeco/Legends|''Legends'' character]] into a pilot seen during the Battle of Yavin in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], identified in the script as Red Twelve,<ref name="TEGW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> and portrayed by Horror film actor [[Chris Matthews]]. In the film, the destruction of [[Theron Nett]] ([[Robert O'Mahoney]])'s starfighter is accompanied by a shot of a different pilot's death,<ref name="ANH" /> which Fry and [[Holocron continuity database|Holocron]] manager [[Leland Chee]] identified as Red Twelve.<ref name="Notes" /> Naeco's helmet prop from the film — or possibly one of a matching design — was later worn by [[Wes Janson]] in ''[[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|The Empire Strikes Back]]''.

Puck was first identified in [[Canon]] by the ''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]''.<ref name="UVG" /> His most prominent appearance thus far, however, has been in ''[[Duty Roster]]'', a part of the ''[[From a Certain Point of View]]'' short story collection penned by Jason Fry, who originally identified the character.<ref name="Duty Roster" />
